chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah from Ubeys ibn Hisham from Salim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Four mosques were renewed in Al-Kufa in happiness for the killing of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him): the Mosque of Al-Ash'ath, and the Mosque of Jarir, and the Mosque of Simak, and the Mosque of Shabas ibn Rabi'.
ai.seo_question: Which four mosques in Kufa were renewed to celebrate the martyrdom of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrates that four prominent mosques in Kufa—associated with Al-Ash'ath, Jarir, Simak, and Shabas ibn Rabi'—were renovated as a gesture of joy following the martyrdom of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). This event highlights the political and social dynamics of the Umayyad period, where key figures utilized religious architecture to celebrate the victory over the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the concept of 'Farah' (joy) in a historical context of triumph over the Prophet's grandson.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abullah, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Four Masjids were renewed in Al-Kufa in happiness of the killing of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> – Masjid Al-Ash’as, and Masjid Jareyr, and Masjid Simak, and Masjid Shabas Bin Rabie’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from Salim who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Four Masjids were rebuilt in Kufa to express happiness for the killing of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam : Al-Ash‘ath and Jarir Masjids, Sammak and Shabath ibn Rib‘i’s Masjids.”
